papers.name: Uncoated
papers.description: No coating at all, so the surface is matt, soft to the touch and faintly toothy. Ink sinks in very slightly, which mutes colour a little and gives printing a quiet, considered look. The easiest of our papers to write on, if guests will be adding a note.

weights.feel: Slim and neat — suits inserts and reply cards
weights.name: Light

weights.feel: Light and fine — for inserts and details cards
weights.name: Featherweight

papers.name: Silk
papers.description: Smooth and lightly coated, with a soft sheen rather than a shine. Ink sits crisply on the surface, so fine type stays sharp and colours keep their depth. The most popular of our papers, and the safest choice if your design carries photographs or fine detail.

weights.feel: Slim and neat — suits inserts and reply cards
weights.name: Light

papers.name: Tintoretto Gesso
papers.description: Made by Fedrigoni in Italy. A finely hammered surface that catches the light as the card turns, in a white that is warm rather than bright. You feel the texture before you read a word, which is most of the reason people choose it.

weights.feel: Fine plaster grain that catches the light
weights.name: Classic

weights.feel: The same plaster grain, light enough to tuck inside
weights.name: Featherweight

papers.name: Nettuno Bianco
papers.description: A Fedrigoni paper with a deep felt marking pressed into both sides in fine parallel lines. Cool white, and clearly textured under the thumb. Type and line work sit beautifully on it; very fine detail and large areas of solid colour rather less so.

weights.feel: Pronounced texture you can feel through the card
weights.name: Classic

papers.name: Acquerello Bianco
papers.description: The tooth of watercolour paper, pressed on both sides, in a soft cream white. It holds ink a little more gently than a smooth sheet, which suits calligraphy and hand-drawn work. Warm, and old-fashioned in the best sense.

weights.feel: Soft watercolour tooth, lovely under calligraphy
weights.name: Classic

papers.name: Sirio Pearl Polar Dawn
papers.description: A pearlescent Fedrigoni paper with the shimmer worked through the sheet rather than coated on top, so it shifts gently as the light moves. Never metallic — closer to the inside of a shell. At its best with simple type, which it flatters.

weights.feel: Shifts gently in the light without looking metallic
weights.name: Classic

papers.name: Recycled Uncoated
papers.description: Wholly recycled and thick with it, with flecks of natural fibre still visible in the surface. Matt, soft and easy to write on. The flecks vary from sheet to sheet, which is the point of it rather than a fault.

weights.feel: Thick and tactile, with visible natural fibre
weights.name: Substantial

papers.name: Cartonboard
papers.description: A rigid board with a bright white printing face and a firm, boardy feel. It holds its shape well and prints cleanly. More upright and businesslike than the softer stocks.

weights.feel: Rigid, with a bright printing surface
weights.name: Classic

papers.name: Ice White
papers.description: A cool, bright white with a silk face. Whites in your design read as genuinely white rather than cream, and colours stay clean and true. The one to choose when the design depends on contrast.

papers.name: Foamex 5mm
papers.description: A PVC foam board, 5mm thick, with a smooth matt face that keeps colour flat and even under venue lighting. It stands on an easel without bowing and does not care about a damp marquee, which is most of the reason signs are made of it rather than paper.

weights.feel: Rigid and waterproof — it will not bow on an easel
weights.name: Standard
